note: A1+ Unit 1 Lesson 1.11 built on 2026-11-18 under the A1+ lesson standards approved 2026-10-27 and the user's 2026-11-09 rule that every A1+ lesson follows up the A1 lesson with the same number. A1 1.11 Friends and People names a husband and wife, their son and daughter and the daughter's friend (The husband and the wife are talking.). The user chose him, her and them as A1+ 1.11's one grammar step on 2026-11-18 and asked for Unit 1 to be completed straight to Preview. The same A1 family does things together: the husband and the wife cook dinner together, the son plays football with his father, the mother reads with the children, and the daughter plays with her friend (A1 1.11's own photo). Each Learn card sets the noun against its pronoun (She cooks dinner with her husband. / She cooks dinner with him.); She plays with her friend. / She plays with her. shows both hers. The Recognize questions reuse 1.9's Who does ... with?, and the photo decides between him, her and them. Banks keep the sentence and change only the final pronoun, which the shared hint explains (with him, con él). A possessive her is always followed by its noun, so a final her is the object pronoun. Three new Flash photos (c01-c03) of A1 1.11's family and one A1 1.11 photo.

lesson.title: 1.11 With him, with her, with them
lesson.unit_outcome: Describe people and family, say what people do every day and how often, and ask about other people’s habits.
lesson.lesson_title: With him, with her, with them
lesson.sub_lesson_title: With him, with her, with them
lesson.goal: Say who people do things with, using him, her and them instead of the person (She cooks dinner with her husband. / She cooks dinner with him.), and answer Who does ... with?
lesson.grammar_function: A follow-up of A1 1.11 Friends and People: A1 names a husband and wife, their son and daughter and a friend (The husband and the wife are talking.); A1+ 1.11 says who they do things with. The one new grammar relationship is the object pronoun after with: him, her and them replace the person (She cooks dinner with her husband. / She cooks dinner with him.), next to the subject pronouns he, she and they. Her is both the possessive (her friend) and the object (with her).
lesson.prerequisite: A1 1.11 husband, wife, son, daughter, friend; A1 1.4 children; A1 1.6 mother, father; A1 3.10 his and her; A1 7.6 play football; A1+ 1.2 reads and the he/she -s (cooks, plays); A1+ 1.4 with; A1+ 1.9 Who does ... with?
lesson.speaking_outcome: Say him, her and them clearly at the end of the sentence, linked to with (with him, with her, with them); the th of them is soft. Do not require native-like speed.
